newsitem.title: USA: S. Africa's Tutu has U.S. hospital checkup.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa's Tutu has U.S. hospital checkup.

text.p: South Africa's Archbishop Desmond Tutu visited urologists at Johns Hopkins Medical Institutions on Thursday for a checkup related to his diagnosed prostate cancer, a Johns Hopkins spokesman said.
"He came for a checkup, he was checked up and he left," Johns Hopkins spokesman Marc Kusinitz said. He said the checkup lasted for about one hour, at the Johns Hopkins outpatient urology clinic.

Kusinitz said Tutu had also visited the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Centre in New York earlier this week. No further information about the Johns Hopkins visit could be released, Kusinitz said, citing patient confidentiality rules.
He said a press conference on Tutu's health would be held in Washington on Friday.

The Baltimore Sun, in an article Thursday, cited a spokesman for Tutu in Cape Town as saying the retired archbishop was seeking additional medical opinion in weighing whether he should have continued treatment through surgery or radio-therapy.
Tutu underwent surgery for a cancerous prostate gland in January, but his surgeons have said additional surgery may be necessary.
Tutu is currently serving as chairman of South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which is trying to lift the veil on apartheid-era human rights abuses.
